newsitem.title: UK: Medeva interim profits seen sharply ahead.
newsitem.headline: Medeva interim profits seen sharply ahead.

text.p: British pharmaceutical Group Medeva Plc is expected on Wednesday to announce a sharp rise in interim pre-tax profits, and the company will be hoping the results give a fillip to the lacklustre performance of its shares.
Analysts' forecasts are for pre-tax profit of between 44.5 and 52.0 million stg, up from 33.9 million a year earlier.
However, the calculation has been a difficult one, with the impact of the surge in sterling and the effect of the June 1996 acquisition of the U.S. assets of the former Fisons clouding the picture.

In a note on Friday, analysts at Lehman Brothers said they had downgraded full-year pre-tax profit forecasts for the company to 119 million stg from 124 million, reflecting an expected exchange rate of $1.70 to the pound in stead of $1.63.

Attention on Wednesday will be focused once more on the performance of its highly profitable behaviour-control drug Methylphenidate, with news still awaited on the emergence of fresh competition in the strictly-controlled U.S. market for the drug, used predominantly in children.

Analysts said reports that giants Eli Lilly and Co (LLY.N, makers of Prozac, and SmithKline Beecham Plc SB.L makers of Paxil/Seroxat, may be looking at extending use of the drugs to children has put a damper on the group's share performance this week.

It has also been undermined by news that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) had issued a warning about heart valve problems linked to another Medeva drug, appetite suppressant Ionamin, when used in conjunction with other products.
The stock has retreated steadily from a March high of 332 pence per share, trading at 256p on Friday afternoon. It touched a 12-month low of 238 pence on Wednesday as news about Ionamin emerged.

However, Daiwa Europe analyst Nigel Keegan said the share price performance was unjustified, with Medeva squeezed in line with many other second-line stocks, as investors concentrated on FTSE 100 issues.
"A lot of people have them on a buy and we are waiting for the shares to go up," he said.

Medeva's shares are trading at less than half the prospective 1997 price/earnings ratio of their larger peers in the UK drugs sector, according to Reuters 3000 data. They are currently on a p/e ratio of 11.27 compared with 28.99 for SmithKline Beecham Plc, 26.49 for Zeneca Group Plc ZEN.L and 24.04 for Glaxo Wellcome Plc GLXO.L. For 1998, this slips to 10.28 times earnings.
Lehman Brothers said that on a price to cash flow basis, Medeva is "even more attractive as the group continues to generate 40 million stg of free cash flow before acquisitions."

Daiwa's Keegan added that worries about competition to Methylphenidate were overdone, while Medeva's Hepatitis B vaccine Hepagene, due to be submitted for regulatory approval next year, also looking a promising product.
